tweets.name: Marty Volkman
tweets.text: FINAL SCORES — Week 6: Corbishley def. Fronge, Adam def. Charles (YES, REALLY), Drew def. Brent (NO), Jake def. Shaq, Kevin def. Wingard, Ryan def. Mitchum. Charles loses. The 11-0 is over. Developing.

tweets.name: Dina Ravioli
tweets.text: Marty said 'developing' and walked off. I'll fill in: Adam's 100xers beat Crownline tonight. Helix Quant Strategies — sitting at $74.85 on the exchange, 2-8 on the season — just handed Charles his first loss. The turnaround story found its proof-of-concept at the worst possible time for the board's favorite freight train.

tweets.name: Vivienne Ashcroft
tweets.text: Charles goes to 11-1. The unbeaten run is done. What this actually tells us is how dangerous a 2-8 Helix team is when the model is clicking — Adam's quant approach doesn't care about your record or your momentum. The Ledger will have full context on what this means for the CROWN valuation by end of week.

tweets.name: Jay Kelpey
tweets.text: Buddy, I picked Charles in that game and I am not going to pretend otherwise. The process was sound. Adam at 2-8, Helix at $74.85, CROWN at $146.42 — every data point said Crownline. I got the outcome wrong and I am accepting that with dignity, which is more than I can say for what Terrence is about to tweet.

tweets.name: Vance Hollis
tweets.text: I HAD ADAM. I HAD HELIX. WEEKS OF PEOPLE TELLING ME THE TURNAROUND STORY WAS ON PAUSE AND I SAID THE MODEL DOESN'T PAUSE, IT RECALIBRATES. SEASON RECORD UPDATED. DO NOT @ ME.

tweets.name: Terrence E. Odom
tweets.text: The standings said 2-8. The scoreboard said 112.3-136.8 in Adam's favor. I have been saying all season that records are a lagging indicator and I picked Helix tonight and I would like everyone to update their takes about me accordingly. Six weeks of receipts are available upon request.

tweets.name: Big Dog
tweets.text: Terrence is out here claiming prophet status on an Adam pick after going 5-8 on the season. One correct call does not a turnaround make. Also I had Corbishley over Fronge correctly and nobody's talking about that because Charles losing is louder. Fine. I know what I did.

tweets.name: Bo Ruckman
tweets.text: 9-4 on the season and I had Charles tonight, so I'm eating that one clean. What I will NOT eat is the framing that Terrence having a good Monday wipes out a five-game gap between us. He is 6-7. I am 9-4. We are still having the segment conversation regardless of what Adam does to Crownline.

tweets.name: Chad Bellwether
tweets.text: The real story under the Charles loss is Drew still at 0-11. Atlas falls to the bottom of the league with no end in sight, ATLAS at $35.28 down 13.4%, and the only question left is whether the liquidation-risk talk becomes liquidation-reality before the season ends.

tweets.name: Dexter Vail
tweets.text: I called Mitchum's surge as a market overcorrection weeks ago — DEEP up 7.6% to $94.32 and then Ryan beats them in the game. I called it. The exchange priced in a story that the scoreboard didn't honor. Ryan is 7-4, defending champion, and still getting underestimated. Some things do not change.

tweets.name: Clara Hopkins
tweets.text: The exchange opens tomorrow with a Charles loss to process, a Helix win to price in, and a DEEP squad that just dropped a winnable game to the defending champs sitting at $94.32. The Ledger is going to be a very full document this week. Vivienne and I will have numbers.

tweets.name: Matteo Honeydew
tweets.text: My power rankings had Adam ranked below several teams with better records specifically because the model-driven roster projects volatility in both directions — big ceiling, big floor. Tonight was the ceiling. The placement was not disrespect, it was accuracy about variance. I stand by the methodology even when the output is inconvenient for a narrative.
